subject: FRE
label: Grade 08
task: Meet the outcome of every unit in Grade 08 French, and keep one piece of evidence for each.
condition: A 36-week school year, 4 units, a teacher or guide, a learning book or device, and local examples in the local language first with English support.
standard: Each unit: at least 8 of 10 marks on a short task, with one line of reasoning for each answer. Course pass: no unit at 'Not yet' after one retry, and a pass in SA1 and SA2.

modules.title: Past and future in simple form
modules.intro: In this unit you work on 'Past and future in simple form', taught in a way that is with notes, a worked line and a self-mark. The target is clear: talk about past and future. You move from seeing it, to saying it, to doing it alone.
points: Listen first: your teacher or a recording says the new words or sentences from 'Past and future in simple form' twice. You repeat them aloud.
Notice the pattern: find where the new sound, word form or sentence rule appears in a short text and mark it.
Use it: talk about past and future, first with help, then alone.
Check and fix: read your work aloud once more; fix one thing you hear is wrong.
modules.example: Solved: Passe compose: j'ai parle, j'ai fini. Futur simple: je parlerai. Method: Model run for 'Past and future in simple form'. Teacher text (3 lines about a daily activity). Step 1, read it aloud together. Step 2, mark every word or sentence that uses the new pattern. Step 3, a learner writes or says two new lines of their own that use the same pattern. Step 4, the learner reads them aloud and corrects one slip. What a good answer looks like: the pattern is used correctly in both lines, the lines make sense, and the learner can say which part is the pattern.
modules.activity: About 30 to 40 minutes of class work, then one short practice task for home. Keep evidence: a worked task and a corrected copy.
modules.standard: Talk about past and future: at least 8 of 10 marks on a short task, with one line of reasoning for each answer.
steps: Step 1, The passé composé talks about finished actions. Form: avoir in the present plus the past participle. J'ai mangé [I ate], tu as fini [you finished], nous avons joué [we played]. Hier, j'ai joué au foot. [Yesterday I played football.]

Step 2, Some verbs use être: aller, arriver, partir, venir, entrer. Je suis allé au marché. [I went to the market, a boy.] Elle est arrivée à huit heures. [She arrived at eight.] With être the participle agrees: allé, allée, allés, allées.

Step 3, The near future uses aller plus the infinitive. Je vais manger. [I am going to eat.] Nous allons jouer demain. [We are going to play tomorrow.] The simple future adds endings to the infinitive: je mangerai, tu finiras, nous jouerons. [I will eat, you will finish, we will play.]

Step 4, Dialogue. Élève A : Qu'est-ce que tu as fait hier ? [What did you do yesterday?] Élève B : J'ai regardé un film. [I watched a film.] Élève A : Et demain ? [And tomorrow?] Élève B : Demain, je jouerai au tennis. [Tomorrow I will play tennis.]

Step 5, Fix errors. A student says j'ai allé. Correction: je suis allé, because aller takes être. Another says je vais mangé. Correction: je vais manger, with the infinitive. A third says elle est allé; correction: elle est allée.

Step 6, Your turn: write yesterday, now and tomorrow with finir. Model answer: Hier, j'ai fini mes devoirs. Aujourd'hui, je finis mon livre. Demain, je finirai mon projet. [Yesterday I finished my homework. Today I finish my book. Tomorrow I will finish my project.]

modules.standard: Describe a day: at least 8 of 10 marks on a short task, with one line of reasoning for each answer.
steps: Step 1, Learn pronominal verbs for the morning. je me réveille [I wake up], je me lève [I get up], je me lave [I wash], je m'habille [I get dressed]. The me stays before the verb. Say: Je me réveille à sept heures. [I wake up at seven.]

Step 2, Add other routine verbs. Je prends le petit déjeuner. [I have breakfast.] Je vais à l'école à huit heures et demie. [I go to school at half past eight.] Je mange à midi. [I eat at noon.] Je rentre à la maison à cinq heures. [I go home at five.]

Step 3, Write the evening. Je fais mes devoirs. [I do my homework.] Je dîne avec ma famille. [I have dinner with my family.] Je me couche à neuf heures. [I go to bed at nine.] Use d'abord, ensuite, puis, enfin for order.

Step 4, Connect in a short paragraph. D'abord, je me réveille à sept heures. Ensuite, je prends le petit déjeuner. Puis je vais à l'école. Enfin, le soir, je me couche tôt. [First I wake up at seven. Then I have breakfast. Then I go to school. Finally in the evening I go to bed early.]

Step 5, Fix errors. A student says je réveille à sept heure. Correction: je me réveille à sept heures. Another writes tu te lèves with je: je te lève; correction: je me lève. Also keep the s on heures when the number is more than one.

Step 6, Your turn: write four sentences about your day with times. Model answer: Je me lève à sept heures. Je vais à l'école à huit heures. Je rentre à quatre heures. Je me couche à dix heures. [I get up at seven. I go to school at eight. I come home at four. I go to bed at ten.]

modules.standard: Follow a longer dialogue: at least 8 of 10 marks on a short task, with one line of reasoning for each answer.
steps: Step 1, Predict before listening. The title is On organise samedi [Planning Saturday]. Expect times, activities and a decision. Draw a three-column table: Qui [who], Quand [when], Quoi [what]. Decide to listen twice: once for the gist, once for the details.

Step 2, Listen for the gist. Read aloud: Léa : Tu es libre samedi ? Tom : Le matin, j'ai un cours de guitare jusqu'à onze heures, mais l'après-midi, je suis libre. Léa : On pourrait aller au cinéma à quinze heures trente. Tom : Bonne idée ! Le film dure combien de temps ? Léa : Une heure quarante. Tom : Alors on sort à dix-sept heures dix. On mange une crêpe après ? Léa : D'accord ! Gist: two friends plan an outing.

Step 3, Fill the table on the second listening. Qui : Léa and Tom. Quand : samedi, 15 h 30 (quinze heures trente). Quoi : cinéma, then une crêpe [a pancake]. Also note Tom's guitar lesson until 11 h (onze heures) and that the film lasts 1 h 40.

Step 4, Check an inference with a calculation. 15 h 30 plus 1 h 40 equals 17 h 10. Tom says dix-sept heures dix, which is correct. When a speaker gives a start time and a length, work out the end time yourself and compare with what you hear.

Step 5, Fix common slips. French often uses the 24-hour clock in speech: quinze heures trente is 3.30 p.m. Do not confuse quinze [15] with quarante [40] or dix-sept [17] with dix-huit [18]. Un quart d'heure [quarter of an hour] is different from quatorze heures [2 p.m.].

Step 6, Your turn: hear Le cours commence à neuf heures quarante-cinq et dure une heure trente. À quelle heure finit-il ? Answer: 9 h 45 plus 1 h 30 is 11 h 15, so il finit à onze heures quinze. [It ends at 11.15.]

modules.standard: Present: at least 8 of 10 marks on a short task, with one line of reasoning for each answer.
steps: Step 1, Pick a topic and a plan. Topic: mon quartier [my neighbourhood]. Plan: introduce, location, what there is, what I like, conclude. A one-minute talk for a language learner at a careful pace is about 60 to 80 words, so about eight to ten short sentences.

Step 2, Build the introduction and location. Bonjour à tous. Je vais vous présenter mon quartier. [Hello everyone. I am going to present my neighbourhood.] D'abord, il est situé près d'un grand parc. [First, it is near a big park.] Je vais plus infinitive is the near future.

Step 3, Add the middle and the opinion. Ensuite, il y a une bibliothèque, un petit marché et deux écoles. [Then there is a library, a small market and two schools.] Enfin, ce que j'aime, c'est le calme et mes amis. [Finally, what I like is the calm and my friends.]

Step 4, Close and deliver. Pour conclure, mon quartier est petit mais agréable. Merci de m'écouter. [To conclude, my neighbourhood is small but pleasant. Thank you for listening.] Use cue cards with one keyword each, look at the audience, and pause for a breath after each sequence word.

Step 5, Fix errors. A child says Je vais présente. Correction: Je vais présenter, because after aller we use the infinitive. Another says il y a un bibliothèque. Correction: une bibliothèque, because it is feminine. Another reads every word; use keywords instead.

Step 6, Your turn: present your school in five sentences. Model answer: Bonjour à tous. Je vais vous présenter mon école. D'abord, elle est près de ma maison. Ensuite, il y a une grande cour et un gymnase. Pour conclure, j'aime mon école parce que mes amis sont là. Merci !

'talk', at the Apply level. (Covered in unit 1: Past and future in simple form.)
When do the formative checks FA1 to FA4 and the summative checks SA1 and SA2 happen?
FA1 to FA4 around weeks 6, 12, 24 and 30; SA1 in week 18; SA2 in week 36. (Covered in: Assessment plan, near the top of this page.)

What evidence do you keep for each unit, and why?
A worked task and a corrected copy. It shows what you can really do and lets a teacher check it against the standard. (Covered in: How you are checked, further down this page.)
ladder: L1: say and read familiar words and short sentences.
L2: read short texts and write connected sentences.
L3: write paragraphs and speak on a topic with notes.
L4: write for different purposes and analyse how texts persuade.
L5: write and argue at length; handle unseen texts.
L6 (degree): academic reading, writing and citation.
L7 (postgraduate): publish, teach or translate with expert accuracy.
